response.explanation: src/domain/subscription.ts imports SystemClock from the outbound adapter layer (line 1). It creates an instance in a field (line 4) and calls clock.now() inside isActive() (line 9). This makes the domain core depend on a concrete infrastructure adapter, which reverses the allowed direction: adapters may depend on the domain, but the domain must not depend on adapters. FF-S01 flags it for that reason. ADR-0002 once allowed this exact import, but it is marked "Superseded by ADR-0009". ADR-0009 is Accepted and says the domain core must not import SystemClock or any other adapter. It must instead depend on a Clock port in src/domain that the outbound adapter implements. The code still follows the old, superseded decision. The fix is small and well defined: add a Clock interface in src/domain, have SystemClock implement it, and inject it into Subscription instead of creating SystemClock inside the class.
